about.title: South Gate Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A faulty product does not need to fail dramatically to upend a household. In South Gate, it might be a space heater that ignites overnight in a home off Southern Avenue, a power tool that kicks back mid-cut, or a child's car seat that unlatches during a collision on Firestone Boulevard. The city recorded 419 injury collisions in 2025, with 597 people hurt, and when a crash injury turns out to involve a tire, airbag, or seat belt that did not perform as designed, the claim can reach well beyond the other driver. California treats these cases under strict liability. You generally need to show the product carried a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your harm, not that anyone was negligent. That puts the product itself at the center of the case, so keep it, along with packaging, receipts, and photos. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why South Gate Residents Use LawProactive for Product Cases

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: Under California law you generally show the product was defective and caused your injury, not that the maker acted carelessly. An attorney who knows this framework can build the claim around the defect itself.

items.title: Several Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the store on Garfield Avenue or Imperial Highway that sold the item may all share liability. Identifying every responsible link in the chain matters for a full recovery.

items.title: Preserving the Product Is Step One
items.desc: The physical item is the core evidence in a defect case, and a connected attorney can guide you on storing it safely and arranging expert inspection before anything is lost or altered.

items.question: My airbag did not deploy in a crash on Imperial Highway in South Gate. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. You may have a claim against the other driver for causing the collision and a separate product liability claim against the vehicle or airbag manufacturer if the system was defective. Keep the car exactly as it is and do not let the insurer salvage it until it has been inspected, because the vehicle is your evidence.

items.question: Do I need to prove the company was careless?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning the injured person generally only needs to show a design, manufacturing, or warning defect existed and that it caused the injury. The manufacturer's level of care is not the central issue in that type of claim.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Hold onto it, along with any packaging, manual, receipt, and photos of the scene and your injuries. Do not repair, return, or throw the item away, even if the retailer offers a refund. An attorney can arrange for it to be examined and can also identify the retailer, distributor, and manufacturer who may each be responsible.
